scope: Generally healthy, nonpregnant adults, assuming no kidney disease, regular medication, other supplements or caffeine. Limits constrain generated portions only; total intake and personal suitability are not screened.

rules.description: Increases preserve all current supplement counts. Decreases alone can remove them. No substitution that erases an existing ball on an increase.
A compound contributes to several goals but its quantity is counted once.
The higher of Sleep/Calm at 0–1 permits up to 75 mg caffeine; at 2 up to 50 mg; at 3 up to 25 mg; at 4–5 none. These are conservative game preference locks, not validated medical cutoffs.

constraints.limitKind: No established tolerable upper intake limit. 3 g is a conservative application portion, not an official safety limit.
constraints.notes: Water-related weight gain or gastrointestinal discomfort may occur. Kidney disease, pregnancy/breastfeeding or medication context require individual review.

assessmentLevels.scope: Single dose, all sources in healthy adults
Daily intake, all sources in healthy nonpregnant adults

constraints.limitKind: EFSA safety assessment levels, not nutrient ULs or recommended targets.
constraints.notes: Other coffee/tea, supplements and stimulants add to exposure. Caffeine can affect sleep, cause jitters or palpitations; use early in the day, at least 8 hours before bedtime. Sensitivity, pregnancy, rhythm conditions and medication context are not screened.

constraints.limitKind: No established UL. The 200 mg application cap reflects short-term trial portions, not a universal safe daily ceiling.
constraints.notes: Long-term daily benefit and suitability are uncertain. Blood-pressure and medication contexts require review. Pregnancy/breastfeeding excluded from assumptions.

constraints.limitKind: US adult UL applies to supplements and medications, excluding naturally occurring food magnesium.

additionalLimits.scope: EU supplemental/added readily dissociable magnesium compounds; naturally present food magnesium excluded

constraints.notes: Diarrhea/nausea possible. Kidney impairment increases toxicity risk. Magnesium can interfere with oral bisphosphonates and tetracycline/quinolone antibiotics; their dose timing requires separation. Diuretics/PPIs can affect magnesium status. Other magnesium products count toward supplemental exposure.
